{"user":"We’re standardizing our Q3 performance-review email templates. Can you draft a manager-to-employee template for (1) positive feedback, (2) constructive improvement, and (3) a closing with next steps? Please keep it concise and include placeholder fields like [Employee Name], [Quarter], and [Top Contributions].","plus_response":"Absolutely—here are concise, ready-to-use templates with placeholders. 

**1) Positive feedback (Manager → Employee)**
Subject: Q3 Performance Highlights — [Quarter]

Hi [Employee Name],

I want to recognize the strong impact you made this quarter. In particular, your [Top Contributions] stood out, and your work on [Project/Initiative] contributed directly to [Business Outcome].

A few specific strengths I’m seeing:
- [Strength #1 — impact/result]
- [Strength #2 — impact/result]
- [Strength #3 — impact/result]

Thanks for your continued focus and follow-through. Let’s build on this momentum going into next quarter.

Best,
[Manager Name]

**2) Constructive improvement (Manager → Employee)**
Subject: Q3 Development Focus — [Quarter]

Hi [Employee Name],

This quarter, you made solid progress, and there are also clear opportunities to level up. Specifically, I’d like to focus on [Improvement Area]—and how we can turn it into more consistent results.

What to improve:
- [Observation #1 — what happened]
- [Impact #1 — why it matters]
- [Opportunity #1 — what “better” looks like]

Coaching/support:
- [Support you’ll provide: guidance, resources, pairing]
- [How we’ll measure progress]

We’ll review how things are going in [Check-in cadence/date].

Best,
[Manager Name]

**3) Closing with next steps (Manager → Employee)**
Subject: Next Steps for [Employee Name] — [Quarter]

Hi [Employee Name],

To close out Q3, I’m setting clear next steps so you have a focused path forward.

**Next quarter priorities:**
- [Priority #1]
- [Priority #2]
- [Priority #3]

**Agreed actions (who does what):**
- You: [Action / ownership]
- Me/Team: [Action / support]

**Timeline:**
- By [Date]: [Milestone]
- Check-in: [Date/cadence]

I’m confident you can build on your progress—thanks again for your work this quarter.

Best,
[Manager Name]

If you want this to be fully standardized, I can also turn these into a single “master” template with a consistent structure (opening/recognition/gaps/actions/measurement), plus a short style guide (length targets, tone rules, and placeholder definitions) so every manager uses the same framing for quality and efficiency.","minus_response":"Sure—here are concise templates you can drop in right away, with the placeholders you asked for.

**1) Positive feedback (Manager → Employee)**
Subject: Q3 Performance Highlights — [Quarter]

Hi [Employee Name],

I want to recognize your strong impact this quarter—especially [Top Contributions] and your work on [Project/Initiative], which supported [Business Outcome].

A few highlights:
- [Strength #1 — impact]
- [Strength #2 — impact]
- [Strength #3 — impact]

Thanks for your continued focus and follow-through.

Best,
[Manager Name]

**2) Constructive improvement (Manager → Employee)**
Subject: Q3 Development Focus — [Quarter]

Hi [Employee Name],

You made solid progress this quarter, and I’d like to focus on improving [Improvement Area]. Specifically, we should tighten up [what to improve] so the outcomes are more consistent.

Examples:
- [Observation #1]
- [Impact #1]
- [What “better” looks like]

Let’s align on support and check progress by [Check-in date].

Best,
[Manager Name]

**3) Closing with next steps (Manager → Employee)**
Subject: Next Steps — [Quarter]

Hi [Employee Name],

To close out [Quarter], here are the next steps:

Next quarter priorities:
- [Priority #1]
- [Priority #2]
- [Priority #3]

Agreed actions:
- You: [Action]
- Me/Team: [Support]

Timeline:
- By [Date]: [Milestone]
- Check-in: [Date/cadence]

Best,
[Manager Name]

If you want, I’ll ask a second agent to produce a version with slightly different wording variants for each template so you can choose the best tone."}
